title: Demo: How Flags Work
description:
Welcome to the Cybersecurity Assessment! A flag is a secret token that proves you solved a question. In this workshop, all flags follow the CTF{...} format.

To test your submission, copy this demo flag and paste it below:

CTF{welcome_to_cyber_workshop_2026}
hint: Highlight the text 'CTF{welcome_to_cyber_workshop_2026}', copy it, paste it into the answer box below, and click Submit Answer.

title: Inspect the Page Source
description:
Every webpage is sent directly to your browser as plaintext HTML. Web developers frequently leave developer notes or staging comments in the HTML markup that users don't normally see on screen.

Press F12 (or Ctrl+Shift+I / Right-click and choose Inspect) to open your browser's Developer Tools. Inspect the HTML markup of this assessment page to find the hidden comment containing the flag!
hint: In Chrome/Firefox/Edge, press F12, go to the 'Elements' tab, and look near the top under the <body> tag for an HTML comment <!-- FLAG: CTF{...} -->.

title: The Base64 Transmission
description:
A communication node intercepted the following Base64-encoded transmission:

Q1RGe2Jhc2U2NF9kZWNvZGluZ19pc19lYXN5fQ==

Base64 is a common encoding scheme that converts binary data into ASCII characters using A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, and /. Decode this string to reveal the secret flag.
hint: In Linux/Termux: echo 'Q1RGe2Jhc2U2NF9kZWNvZGluZ19pc19lYXN5fQ==' | base64 -d. Or in Python: import base64; print(base64.b64decode('Q1RGe...').decode())

title: Caesar's Cipher (ROT-13)
description:
Julius Caesar encrypted confidential military orders by rotating letters of the alphabet by a fixed distance. The text below was encrypted using ROT-13 (each letter shifted forward by 13 positions):

PGS{ebg13_pvcure_fhpprff_2026}

Rotate each letter by 13 positions (for example: P rotates 13 back to C, G rotates to T, S rotates to F) to uncover the flag.

title: Malicious Server Log
description:
Security analysts detected an intrusion attempt on our web server. Below is the relevant excerpt from the access log:

192.168.1.15 - - [16/Sep/2026:10:12:01] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 4210
192.168.1.15 - - [16/Sep/2026:10:12:04] "GET /css/style.css HTTP/1.1" 200 1420
192.168.1.99 - - [16/Sep/2026:10:12:18] "POST /cgi-bin/test.sh?cmd=CTF{grep_finds_the_needle_in_haystack} HTTP/1.1" 200 180
192.168.1.15 - - [16/Sep/2026:10:12:22] "GET /favicon.ico HTTP/1.1" 404 280

Identify the malicious request and extract the embedded flag.
hint: Look at line 3: the attacker sent a POST request to /cgi-bin/test.sh with a cmd parameter containing the flag.

title: Binary Byte Stream
description:
Computers store characters as 8-bit binary numbers. An emergency signal transmitted the following sequence of ASCII bytes:

01000011 01010100 01000110 01111011 01100010 01101001 01110100 01110011 01111101

Translate each 8-bit binary group into its ASCII character to recover the flag (e.g. 01000011 = 67 = 'C').
